summary: PulseGuard v0.6.5 removes the custom three-minute burn-in experiment and replaces it with a fast evidence-only Hardware Health Check. Sound, video/FPS, synthetic CPU/GPU/RAM stress, temperature-driver/PawnIO downloads and sensor-provider setup are removed. The release also safely cleans stale partial-download remnants and fixes the protection sidebar so it resolves real-time status without requiring a Full Health Scan.

sections.heading: Hardware Health Check
sections.detail: Checks only evidence PulseGuard can prove reliably: Windows storage health, recent WHEA hardware events, BSOD history, Device Manager/driver health, LAN/network state and battery health on laptops. No synthetic CPU/GPU/RAM burn-in is performed; extended burn-in belongs in a dedicated tool such as BurnInTest.

sections.heading: Removed unreliable test surface
sections.detail: The sound test, custom video/FPS decoder test, custom 2D/3D stress loop, temperature card, LibreHardwareMonitor/PawnIO sensor-provider download path and three-minute worker are removed rather than kept as noisy or misleading diagnostics.

sections.heading: Cleaner partial-download handling
sections.detail: Deep Clean may remove only real *.crdownload, *.part, *.partial and *.download files in the current user's Downloads folder when they are older than 12 hours. Completed downloads and all other Downloads content remain protected.

sections.heading: Protection status UI fix
sections.detail: The real-time protection sidebar now shows CHECKING briefly and performs a lightweight Defender status query after the window opens, instead of leaving NOT SCANNED until a Full Health Scan is run.

sections.heading: Launcher/release hardening
sections.detail: VBScript launchers are emitted without a BOM, and obsolete v0.6.4 video/sensor files exist only as tiny transition placeholders when required by the older updater; v0.6.5 removes them after the new runtime is active.
